svg.title: Backups: independent copies.
svg.desc: A backup is an independent copy used to recover lost data. An illustrative two-device diagram shows a computer holding note.txt with hello and a local hidden .git history directory, and an older saved copy on a separate backup device or location chosen by the reader. The working file later gains again. When the computer disk fails, both its file and local history are lost together; restoring the independent older copy yields hello, not the uncopied again line. Backups must keep older copies rather than merely mirror deletions, include needed untracked and ignored data, and include .git if local history is wanted. A remote Git copy protects only pushed commits, not every local file. Make regular independent copies and verify restoration into a spare directory without overwriting originals. Protect private backup data; secrets need not be committed.
svg.text: A backup is an independent copy for recovering lost data.
Files and history can be lost together. Another directory on the same disk is not enough.
Example contents. Keep regular, older copies, not just a mirror of deletions.
Include needed files Git does not track or ignores; .git keeps local history.
Git records committed files; a remote Git copy protects pushed commits only.
Verify restore into a spare directory. Protect private copies; don't commit secrets.
